::: {#sol-valid-arguments}

1. Yes.
   $P \Rightarrow Q$ is false when $P$ is true and $Q$ is false (@def-implies),
   so if $P \Rightarrow Q$ and $P$ are both true, $Q$ is true.
2. No.
   If the tests fail but someone deploys the build by hand,
   $P$ is false and $Q$ is true.
   Then $P \Rightarrow Q$ and $Q$ are both true, and $P$ is false.
3. Yes.
   $\neg Q$ is true, so $Q$ is false (@def-not).
   If $P$ were true, $P \Rightarrow Q$ would be false,
   so $P$ is false and $\neg P$ is true.
4. Yes.
   $\neg R$ is true, so $R$ is false (@def-not).
   $P \lor R$ is true only if $P$ or $R$ is true (@def-or),
   so $P$ is true.

:::
